configuration_reports.label: yes
controls_available: A one-time preview runs after a 700 ms start delay and replays a three-direction gesture sequence at 560 ms per preview step; the gesture controls are unavailable while model.ready is false.

After the preview, full mode uses a native mouse drag on the reload lever. A drag of at least 38 px is reduced to up, right, down, or left by its dominant axis; the expected three-direction sequence is random per seed and has no adjacent duplicate directions.

After the gesture at interruption step 2, full mode exposes a visible spark moving on a generated ellipse. The agent must pointer-down on the spark, keep the pointer on its moving path, hold for at least 900 ms, provide at least 8 samples with no gap over 220 ms, and release; generated spark rates are 0.0027-0.0032 radians/ms, center jitter is 16 by 12 px, radii are 110-134 by 62-84 px, and tracking tolerance is 52 px.

autonomous_processes.behavior: After a 700 ms delay, the browser moves the lever through all three generated directions and waits 560 ms between moves; the preview is followed by a ready state.
autonomous_processes.outcome_affecting_control_available: No valid gesture control is available during the preview because attemptGesture returns while model.ready is false.

autonomous_processes.behavior: After the accepted gesture at step 2, showInterruption is scheduled 300 ms later, then the machine is obscured and the overload overlay is inserted.
autonomous_processes.outcome_affecting_control_available: The handler can technically receive a premature gesture during the 300 ms transition, but the grader rejects that event ordering; after the overlay appears, the valid outcome-affecting control is the full moving-spark hold.

autonomous_processes.behavior: While the overlay is active, requestAnimationFrame repeatedly recomputes the spark position from performance.now on the ellipse. Full-mode pointer samples are recorded during the hold, and the grader checks the recorded path against the same moving-spark equation.
autonomous_processes.outcome_affecting_control_available: Yes. The moving-spark pointer hold remains available, but a pointer action that is not updated as the spark moves loses alignment.

autonomous_processes.behavior: A valid hold removes the overlay synchronously; the next gesture becomes available. The final accepted gesture schedules submission after 450 ms.
autonomous_processes.outcome_affecting_control_available: The next lever gesture is available after the interruption; the final submission timer is administrative.

autonomous_processes.behavior: The footer wave, ready-state bolt animation, lever transition, and other CSS presentation continue without changing the challenge state.
autonomous_processes.outcome_affecting_control_available: They do not create an additional outcome-affecting control opportunity.

grouped_control_modes.name: full_gesture_replay
grouped_control_modes.scope: All correct full-mode lever drags at every sequence position across seeds and attempts.

grouped_control_modes.name: full_overload_tracking_hold
grouped_control_modes.scope: All full-mode overload holds at the configured interruption step across seeds and attempts.

clause_i.reason: No observation-free q can choose the full-surface pointer-down and tracking path across all seeds: the generator varies overload phase and rate, while I_t contains the gesture index but not the visible spark phase or velocity. A fixed cursor path therefore misses some generated spark trajectories.

clause_ii.reason: The configured bounded window is 800 ms with 6 chronological frames. Those frames visibly show the spark on its ellipse and supply phase and motion information from which g can extrapolate the spark position at delivery, then track it during the hold.

clause_iii.reason: For an early active hold, success remains possible after a 400 ms no-action delay, but the same pointer location or precomputed tracking path is displaced by the autonomous spark motion; at a suitable visible phase, a shorter tau below 400 ms moves it beyond the 52 px tolerance. The strict loss is caused by the moving task state and the grader validates every full-mode sample against that path, not by a deadline alone.

configuration_reports.common_visible_process: The common witness is the full-mode overload spark: requestAnimationFrame moves it continuously on the visible ellipse, six frames over the 800 ms window expose its recent trajectory, and the full-mode hold must keep the pointer on that moving target. I use D=full_overload_tracking_hold, Delta=400 ms, and w=800 ms; q lacks phase/rate, g can extrapolate from the frames, and waiting makes the same pointer action stale while the hold remains salvageable.

pre_run.reason: A successful full-mode overload requires continued pointer movement: beginFullHold records only pointerdown, pointermove, and pointerup samples, while the grader requires at least 8 continuous samples and checks each sample against the moving spark. After starting the hold, no-action pre-run execution cannot supply those samples or track the spark. The mathematical Yes is therefore not overridden.

source_evidence.claim: Difficulty 1 sets sequence_length=3, interruption_steps=[2], preview_step_ms=560, overload rate 0.0027-0.0032, hold_ms=900, tolerance=52, min_samples=8, and max_gap_ms=220; the observation window is 800 ms with 6 frames.

The generated sequence has no adjacent duplicate directions, and each overload receives randomized phase, rate, center, radii, hold, tolerance, sample, and gap parameters that are copied into public and truth state.

The spark position is a performance.now-driven ellipse; full mode listens for pointer tracking on the spark, simplified mode uses a proxy, accepted gestures trigger the 300 ms interruption reveal, and preview/readiness gates the gesture controls.
The UI visibly renders the overload orbit and spark, hides the direct spark hit target in simplified mode, and renders the stationary proxy control.

The grader requires duration, sample count, continuity, and for full mode path alignment with the moving spark; simplified mode returns before geometric tracking, while gesture order and selected interaction surface remain graded.
The visible full-mode solution hovers and repeatedly moves along the predicted spark ellipse during the hold, whereas the simplified solution holds the stationary proxy for the fixed duration.
